children: Federal Reserve Economic Data has launched Model Context Protocol Connector to address risks and challenges arising from AI visitors, according to the Federal Reserve Board Governor Christopher Waller.
Waller was speaking on "Federal Reserve Economic Data" before the event, "FRED Con: Navigating Trust, AI & Storytelling in a World of Data".
"AI can hallucinate, introduce bias, and hide key assumptions, often with confidence and polish," said Waller.

"This risk has implications for FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) and its role as the reliable source of data produced by other organizations. AI may not accurately cite the sources for data. AI may also make a variety of errors in interpreting data, such as that old
for economists and statisticians—confusing correlation with causation."
"Another challenge that we are dealing with is an onslaught of traffic growth," said the Fed governor and FOMC voting member.

"FRED traffic has always tended to grow each year, but the pace has picked up since the advent of AI. It is presently growing 150 percent a year, with most of that growth from AI and bots. Already about half of visits to FRED are from AI agents retrieving data, with the other half from flesh-and-blood visitors," he noted.

"One challenge for us in understanding these AI visits is that FRED's managers don't know whether AI agents are correctly attributing data to the original source, or to FRED, as we have sometimes seen in testing," he said, adding that AI agents are generally very accurate.
"In response to these challenges and opportunities, FRED has introduced the FRED MCP (Model Context Protocol) Connector to simplify connecting FRED data with AI systems."

"Up till now, FRED has been designed to be viewed and understood by humans. But an AI bot sees and interprets data very differently. And that means the FRED team must adapt how FRED is presented to this new type of viewer so that the data are conveyed back to the agent's master accurately and in a well-documented manner."
Additionally, the FRED staff is developing skills to help AI agents understand and work with economic data more effectively and accurately.

title: Federal Reserve Economic Data launches tool to address risks, challenges from AI visits
